name: latexshock
description: Triggers an OpenShock shocker based on LaTeX (and general Problems-panel) compile results. Intensity and duration reflect how badly the compile went.

commands.title: LaTeXShock: Send Test Shock (power 1, 300ms, ignores enabled)

latexShock.enabled.description: Master switch. When off, no shocks are ever sent. Defaults to off so nothing happens until you opt in.

latexShock.dryRun.description: When on, compute and log what would be sent but never contact the OpenShock API. Useful for tuning weights and curves safely.

enumDescriptions: One shock per dirty compile, with intensity/duration scaled by the weighted severity score.
One short pulse per issue (capped at pulses.maxCount), spaced by at least the safety cooldown.
latexShock.mode.description: How a 'compiled but dirty' result is delivered. Compile failures are always a single binary shock regardless of this setting.

latexShock.connection.apiBaseUrl.description: Base URL of the OpenShock API (or a self-hosted instance).

latexShock.connection.shockerId.description: The OpenShock shocker ID to activate. The API token is stored separately via the 'LaTeXShock: Set OpenShock API Token' command, not in settings.

latexShock.build.taskFilter.description: Case-insensitive regex matched against a finished task's name, source, and type to decide whether its exit code counts as a LaTeX build. A non-zero exit from a matching task is treated as a compile failure.

enumDescriptions: Use the VS Code Problems panel (works with LaTeX Workshop and any linter).
Parse a LaTeX .log file directly; skip if none is found.
Parse a .log file if one can be found, otherwise fall back to diagnostics.
latexShock.diagnostics.source.description: Where 'compiled but dirty' issue counts come from.

latexShock.diagnostics.logPath.description: Explicit path to the LaTeX .log file to parse when diagnostics.source is 'log' or 'auto'. Supports ${workspaceFolder}. When empty, LaTeXShock looks next to the active document, then for the most recently modified *.log in the workspace.

enumDescriptions: Only score diagnostics after a build task matching build.taskFilter finishes.
Also score diagnostics whenever they change, with no build task involved.
latexShock.diagnostics.evaluateOn.description: When a 'compiled but dirty' evaluation may run. 'buildTask' ties shocks to actual builds. Use 'anyChange' only if your builder never runs as a VS Code task (e.g. LaTeX Workshop's internal build) - diagnostics change constantly while you type, so this can fire without you building anything.

latexShock.diagnostics.includeNonLatexFi.description: Count diagnostics from files that aren't LaTeX sources (.tex/.ltx/.bib/.sty/.cls/.dtx/.ins). Enables the generalized 'any language in the Problems panel' use case, but lets unrelated linters anywhere in the workspace drive the shock.

latexShock.triggers.compileFailure.description: Shock on a hard compile failure (build task exits non-zero / no PDF produced).

latexShock.triggers.undefinedReferences.description: Count undefined references/citations toward the severity score.

latexShock.triggers.overfullHbox.description: Count overfull hbox warnings toward the severity score.

latexShock.triggers.underfullHbox.description: Count underfull hbox warnings toward the severity score.

latexShock.triggers.packageWarnings.description: Count package / generic LaTeX warnings toward the severity score.

latexShock.triggers.fontWarnings.description: Count font warnings toward the severity score.

latexShock.weights.compileFailure.description: Severity contribution of a compile failure (used for scaling; failures also honor power.failureOverride).

latexShock.weights.packageWarning.description: Severity contribution per package / generic warning.

latexShock.power.min.description: Minimum shock intensity (0-100) for a scaled 'compiled but dirty' event.

latexShock.power.max.description: Maximum shock intensity (0-100) for a scaled 'compiled but dirty' event, before the safety ceiling.

latexShock.power.failureOverride.description: Intensity used for a hard compile failure. A failure is a binary event and always uses this value (still clamped by the safety ceiling).

latexShock.duration.minMs.description: Minimum shock duration in milliseconds for a scaled event.

latexShock.duration.maxMs.description: Maximum shock duration in milliseconds for a scaled event.

latexShock.duration.failureMs.description: Duration in milliseconds for a hard compile failure.

latexShock.scaling.curve.description: How the weighted severity score maps to output. linear: proportional. logarithmic: diminishing returns for piling up errors. exponential: punishes piling up harder. stepped: discrete tiers (see scaling.stepThresholds).

latexShock.scaling.target.description: Which dimension the severity score scales. The non-scaled dimension is held at its configured minimum.

latexShock.scaling.referenceScore.description: The weighted severity score at which scaled output saturates to its maximum. Lower values make the extension reach max intensity/duration sooner.

latexShock.scaling.stepThresholds.description: Weighted-score thresholds defining tiers when scaling.curve is 'stepped'. Each threshold crossed moves output one tier higher between min and max.

latexShock.pulses.intensity.description: Intensity (0-100) of each pulse when mode is 'pulses'. Clamped by safety.hardMaxPower.

latexShock.pulses.durationMs.description: Duration in milliseconds of each pulse when mode is 'pulses'.

latexShock.pulses.maxCount.description: Maximum number of pulses emitted for a single dirty compile when mode is 'pulses'.

latexShock.pulses.spacingMs.description: Requested gap in milliseconds between pulses when mode is 'pulses'. The effective gap is never smaller than safety.cooldownMs.

latexShock.safety.hardMaxPower.description: Absolute intensity ceiling enforced regardless of any other setting.

latexShock.safety.cooldownMs.description: Minimum time in milliseconds between activations. Shocks requested during the cooldown window are dropped, never queued.
